title: How haunted is SLO County? Ghost sightings, phantom phone calls and more
excerpt: From ghostly figures to creepy noises, here's what locals say they've seen and heard.
content:
Reported by Stephanie Zappelli and Alexiah Syrai Olsen, with AI summarization

Sat, October 31, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC

2 min read

From a mission linked to a mass murder to haunted hotels and homes, San Luis Obispo County is full of ghost stories.

Locals and visitors have reported strange sights, sounds and phone calls at several spots across the region.

Unexplained phenomena include ghost sightings,

FULL STORY: Do spirits haunt these SLO County spots? Here are 7 local ghost stories

Here are key takeaways:

  • Mission Prep ghosts: Author and retired teacher Jim Gregory has written about "repeated sister sightings" at Mission College Preparatory Catholic High School, which once housed Catholic nuns as the Academy of the Immaculate Heart of Mary. Other strange occurrences include an exploding light bulb and phantom construction noises.

  • Mission San Miguel murders: In 1848, 11 people were murdered at Mission San Miguel Arcangel. Men staying at the mission overheard owner William Reed bragging about buried gold, and killed him and his family. Visitors have reported seeing ghosts, including a man in a navy pea coat and a little boy with an "owie" on his neck.

  • Paso Robles hotel's phantom caller: Front desk staff at Paso Robles Inn have received unexplained calls from Room 1007. Local legend ties them to J.H. Emsley, who warned guests of a 1940 fire at the original hotel and reportedly died of a heart attack that night.

  • Sunny Acres: Before Bishop Street Studios became a housing complex, the San Luis Obispo site housed the Sunny Acres orphanage and a juvenile detention facility. People have reported hearing phantom children's laughter, echoing footsteps and doors slamming on their own.

  • Adelaida Cemetery: A spectral woman in a pink dress can be seen wandering the cemetery west of Paso Robles after dark, weeping. The Pink Lady may be the ghost of Charlotte Sitton, a grief-stricken mother who died by suicide in 1890.

  • Bluebird Inn in Cambria: George Lull built the Cambria motel in 1880 as a home for his second wife, Mary Inman Lull. Hotel guests described seeing Mary's ghost, clad in a white gown, floating through the parking lot and garden late at night.

The summary points above were compiled with the help of AI tools and edited by journalists. The full story in the link at top was reported, written and edited entirely by journalists.
